definitions.explanation: The moment or period right before something happens. Emphasizes very close temporal proximity.

examples.japanese: {出発|しゅっぱつ}{直前|ちょくぜん}に{電話|でんわ}が{来|き}た。
examples.english: A phone call came just before departure.

examples.japanese: {試験|しけん}の{直前|ちょくぜん}まで{勉強|べんきょう}していた。
examples.english: I was studying right up until just before the exam.

examples.japanese: {締|し}め{切|き}り{直前|ちょくぜん}になってようやくレポートを{書|か}き{始|はじ}めるのは{悪|わる}い{癖|くせ}だ。
examples.english: It's a bad habit to only start writing the report just before the deadline.

notes:
USAGE:
Used as a temporal noun, typically in the patterns ～の{直前|ちょくぜん} (just before ~) or ～{直前|ちょくぜん} (immediately before ~, as a compound). Can also be used with に: {直前|ちょくぜん}に (at the last moment). The の is often dropped in compound forms: {出発|しゅっぱつ}{直前|ちょくぜん} = just before departure.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {出発|しゅっぱつ}{直前|ちょくぜん}: just before departure
- {試験|しけん}{直前|ちょくぜん}: just before an exam
- {締|し}め{切|き}り{直前|ちょくぜん}: just before the deadline
- {直前|ちょくぜん}に{中止|ちゅうし}する: to cancel at the last minute

CONTRAST:
- {直後|ちょくご}: immediately after (the opposite)
